Lu, “Thru-the-wall eavesdropping on loudspeakers via rfid by capturing sub-mm level vibration,” Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies, vol. 5, no. 4, pp. 1–25, 2021.
paper_level_summary_zh: 本文在相关工作中简要提及RFID-based voice detection方法，将目标论文作为RFID代表工作之一，未给予特殊地位或详细评价。

evidences.evidence_quote: Existing efforts include mmWave-based voice detection [1]–[6], RFID-based voice detection [7]–[9], and UWB-based voice detection [10].
evidences.evidence_context: Since voice-based acoustic signals are easily blocked by soundproof materials, direct acoustic eavesdropping from outside a private space is often infeasible. As a result, Radio Frequency (RF)-based communication and sensing technologies have been explored in increasingly sophisticated forms for eavesdropping applications. Existing efforts include mmWave-based voice detection [1]–[6], RFID-based voice detection [7]–[9], and UWB-based voice detection [10]. While these systems demonstrate the potential of RF signals to recover speech, their practical applications are constrained to controlled environments and lack robustness in real-world scenarios.

evidences.why_this_judgment_zh: 目标论文被归入RFID-based voice detection [7]–[9]中，虽然[7]和[8]可能是其他RFID工作，但[21]是RFID代表作之一。引用论文承认RFID具备语音检测能力，但未单独突出目标论文的亚毫米级精度或through-wall能力；属于general capability recognition，且attribution risk较低。
evidences.copy_ready_zh: 引用论文指出RFID-based方法可用于声音窃听，目标论文属于RFID语音检测的代表作之一。
